title: Raising the House
hook: Ibrahim and Isma'il raise the foundations of the House, praying, accept this from us

segments.voice: Yesterday: the dream, and a ransom before the knife fell. Your line was the test was the willingness. Did you give the small thing up? Day forty-two, the end of the week, and the last day with Ibrahim.

If you've ever built something with your father, or your kid, you know it's never really about the shelf. One holds the board, one drives the screw, someone drops the level, somebody laughs. The thing gets built, and something else gets built too. Now go back to the valley that had nothing in it. There's a spring there now, and people have come to live around it. Ibrahim comes back, and Isma'il is a grown man, sharpening arrows by the water. And Ibrahim says, Allah has commanded me to build a House here. Will you help me? And his son says yes. Today's word is what they built.
screen: `BUILDING WITH YOUR FATHER.` → `THE VALLEY HAS A SPRING NOW.` → `WILL YOU HELP ME?`

segments.voice: The Ka'ba. It's a plain, cube-shaped stone building in the center of the great mosque in Mecca, draped in black cloth. The Qur'an tells believers, wherever they are, to turn their faces toward it in prayer. That direction is called the qibla. So when a Muslim in Chicago or Jakarta faces one way on a prayer rug, this is the way. The Qur'an, in Surah al-Baqarah, gives us the building site. Ibrahim and Isma'il are raising the foundations of the House, and as they work, they pray: our Lord, accept this from us. You are the Hearer, the Knower. Notice what they don't say. Not look what we built. Not remember our names. Accept it from us. The builders ask only that the work be received. The hadith in Bukhari adds the texture: Isma'il carries the stones and Ibrahim sets them, and when the wall grows too high, Ibrahim stands on a stone to keep building. That stone is still there, near the Ka'ba, called the Station of Ibrahim, and the Qur'an says to take the place where Ibrahim stood as a place of prayer. Some traditions say the House was first founded long before Ibrahim, even by Adam, and that Ibrahim raised it again. The Qur'an says he raised its foundations. And look how this week's stories meet here. The valley where Hajar asked her question. The spring where she ran. The son who said do what you are commanded. It all becomes one place. Ibrahim started these eleven days looking at a star, a moon, a sun, and loving what doesn't set. He ends it facing one House.
screen: `A CUBE OF STONE — AND THE QIBLA.` · `OUR LORD, ACCEPT THIS FROM US.` · `THE STATION OF IBRAHIM.` · `THE WEEK MEETS IN ONE PLACE.` · then, large: `KA'BA.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: build something small. Stack three books. Fold a napkin. Line up the pens on your desk. Make your bed properly. Something your hands can finish in a minute. As you do it, go slowly, and put the whole of yourself into one small job. If you pray, you can say, as they did, our Lord, accept this from us. If you don't, just notice what it feels like to make something without needing anyone to see it. The bell holds the time.
Ka'ba. The cube-shaped House in Mecca that Ibrahim and Isma'il raised, and that Muslims face in every prayer. Today's word.

Your line: accept it from us. Eleven days with Ibrahim: the stars, the idols, the fire, the guests, the valley, the spring, the dream, the House. Tonight, do one job well and ask for nothing back. Day forty-two.

screen: `DAY 42 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: A BASKET ON THE RIVER.`

howItsDone: Muslims face the Ka'ba in Mecca for each of the five daily prayers, a direction called the qibla; pilgrims on Hajj and Umrah walk around it seven times and pray near the Station of Ibrahim.

original.note: Arabic: the Ka'ba, the cube-shaped House in Mecca.

trapdoor: what you thought: a black box Muslims pray to.
what it means: a House raised by Ibrahim and Isma'il for the worship of the One God. Muslims face it in prayer; they pray to Allah, not to the building.
what a scholar hears: 2:127 has them raising al-qawa'id, the foundations, and some traditions say the House was first founded before Ibrahim, even by Adam.

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 3364 (Ibrahim returns; Isma'il helps build; the stone)
Qur'an 2:144 (turning toward the Sacred Mosque in prayer)

notes: 2:127 paraphrased ('our Lord, accept this from us; You are the Hearer, the Knower'), not quoted.

Details from the long Bukhari hadith (3364, from memory): Isma'il found sharpening arrows near Zamzam, Ibrahim asking his help, Isma'il carrying stones and Ibrahim standing on a stone as the wall rose. Please confirm.
Meaning of Ka'ba: commonly explained as 'cube' (from ka'b); stated as 'something like a cube'. Confirm.
Pre-Ibrahim founding (Adam): stated as 'some traditions say'; confirm framing.
The trapdoor's second floor clarifies that Muslims pray to Allah, not to the building; confirm the Keeper wants this stated.
Week-end and Ibrahim-part look-back in the teach and carry (days 32–42).

Editor review 2026-10-01: the carry said 'twelve days with Ibrahim'; the Ibrahim part is days 32–42, eleven days, so the carry and teach now say eleven. Cut the etymology of Ka'ba (now described as cube-shaped, not 'the word means'), 'Muslims everywhere / five times a day' (now 2:144's wherever you are), 'the best builders', and 'people have faced it ever since' (the Muslim qibla was first toward Jerusalem). 2:125 now rendered as 'take the place where Ibrahim stood as a place of prayer'.
